title: Isolated cohort contrast testing for pin rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Validate new model revisions behind existing user-visible pins using isolated, low-volume cohorts that exercise production traffic slices while keeping the pin population unaffected. This ticket defines a lightweight, pin-aware canary approach that publishes model performance profiles, enforces cost and latency budgets, and enables automated rollback triggers. The work touches model onboarding flows, release metadata publishing, routing policy updates, telemetry dashboards, and a short playbook for operators.
acceptance_criteria: Create a pin-aware canary stage that routes <=1% of production queries from targeted cohorts to the candidate model without altering the pinned users' default variant.
Performance profile for candidate model is published to the model catalog and surfaced in the Console before any ramp.
Gates enforce: 95th latency <= 1.5x baseline, token-cost delta <= +20%, and quality regression signals below configured thresholds for two defined prompt sets.
Automated rollback and fallback to pinned variant on gate breach with observable incident in Console and alerting to on-call.
Runbook and dashboard widgets for the experiment are documented and linked in the ticket.
plan: Align on scope with Eng, Runtime, and DX: define cohorts, traffic shaping, and required telemetry (2d)
Extend onboarding flow to publish a minimal performance profile snapshot (latency distribution, p50/p95, tokens-per-request estimate) when a revision is uploaded (3d)
Add routing policy option: 'pin-aware-isolated-cohort' that can attach to a pin without changing pin's default mapping (4d)
Create Console experiment card and telemetry dashboard for cohort-level metrics (2d)
Run closed production dry-run (mirror mode) for one day, analyze signals, then flip to 0.5% live traffic for 48h (2d + 2d)
Document playbook and automated rollback thresholds in the runbook (1d)
rollout_plan: Step 0 — Dry run: mirror 100% of cohort traffic to candidate model into a separate telemetry stream (no user-visible effect) and validate instrumentation.
Step 1 — Micro-cohort: route 0.1% of eligible cohort traffic (bounded by user hashing) to candidate model for 24h. Observe base metrics.
Step 2 — Extended micro: increase to 0.5% for 48h if all gates pass. Compare against pinned-variant control cohort.

Step 3 — Decision point: if gates pass for both quality and SLOs, mark candidate as 'verified' and prepare larger staged ramps (handled in follow-up ticket). If any gate fails, automated fallback returns traffic to pinned variant and alerts on-call.
Fallback behavior: immediate failover to pinned variant; background job records affected requests to facilitate root-cause analysis.
metrics: Latency p50/p95 for candidate vs pinned cohort (ms)
Token cost delta per request (estimated cost model)
Normalized quality delta on canonical prompt sets (BLEU/ROUGE-style and custom eval heuristics)
Error rate and top exception classes
Cache hit ratio, KV-delta for candidate vs baseline
Per-cohort throughput and tail queuing metrics
risks: Instrumentation gaps: missing or delayed telemetry could cause false negatives/positives on gates.
Cohort leakage: misrouting could impact pinned users if routing policy is misconfigured.
Cost uplift: micro-cohorts increase inference spend; need to budget for experiments.
Quality signal sparsity: for low-frequency prompts, regressions may be hard to detect in small cohorts.
